claim: Pre-trained Pre-Norm LLMs can be approximated as linear Pre-Norm systems.
falsifier: Verify the linear approximation by measuring the deviation from linearity in pre-trained Pre-Norm LLMs.

conditions: Based on Theorem E.1 and Theorem E.2
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal derivation and the specific assumptions of the theorems; transfer to other architectures is unestablished.

title: Pre-trained Pre-Norm LLMs–Approximability as linear Pre-Norm theorem

claim: Augmenting the action space of deep reinforcement learning agents with conventions—sequences of cooperative actions spanning multiple time steps and agents—improves task performance, training speed, and converged score in cooperative multi-agent environments compared to using only primitive actions.
falsifier: In a cooperative multi-agent environment with a fixed set of primitive actions, implement an augmented action space that includes a set of predefined conventions. Train agents using the same deep RL algorithm (e.g., DQN) with and without the convention space, and compare their final scores, training time, and variance across multiple seeds.

conditions: agents are trained via deep reinforcement learning (e.g., DQN, Rainbow)
the environment is a cooperative multi-agent task (e.g., Hanabi)
conventions are appended to the primitive-action space to form an augmented action-convention space
agents do not explicitly communicate which convention is being followed; they observe only the environment action determined by the convention policy
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (Hanabi), population (DQN/Rainbow agents), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Augmentation of the action for task performance, faster training
